block1.tip: Anak kalimat yang subjeknya sama dengan subjek klausa utama bisa diringkas. Gunakan V-ing untuk makna aktif atau sedang berlangsung, dan V3 untuk makna pasif atau selesai.

youtube.videoDescription: Video 10 sampai 15 menit tentang anak kalimat yang diringkas menjadi frasa V-ing dan V3, dengan contoh participle dan gerund.

lesson.intro: Anak kalimat yang panjang sering bisa diringkas menjadi frasa. Frasa itu lebih singkat, tetapi tetap memberi informasi yang sama. Kunci utamanya adalah subjek yang sama dan bentuk kata kerja yang tepat.

sections.heading: V-ing untuk makna aktif
sections.bodyMd: Jika anak kalimat bermakna aktif atau sedang berlangsung, gunakan **V-ing**: **The student who is sitting by the window is my friend.** menjadi **The student sitting by the window is my friend.**

sections.heading: V3 untuk makna pasif
sections.bodyMd: Jika anak kalimat bermakna pasif atau selesai, gunakan **V3**: **The house, which was built in 1900, has a garden.** menjadi **The house built in 1900 has a garden.**

sections.heading: Gerund dan participle
sections.bodyMd: **Gerund** adalah kata benda dari kata kerja -ing: **Reading is my hobby.** Participle adalah bentuk -ing atau V3 yang menerangkan kata benda atau memendekkan anak kalimat: **Leaving the room, she smiled.**

block3.title: Mengurangi Kata dalam Kalimat
block3.text:
Writers often shorten long sentences by using reduced clauses. A reduced clause is a clause that has been shortened, usually to a participle phrase. For example, The student who is sitting by the window is my friend can be reduced to The student sitting by the window is my friend. The participle phrase sitting by the window describes the student.

A present participle ends in -ing, while a past participle usually ends in -ed or uses a third form such as written or built. Present participles often replace active clauses, and past participles often replace passive clauses. Consider the sentence The house, which was built in 1900, has a large garden. It can be reduced to The house built in 1900 has a large garden.

Being and having can also appear in reduced clauses. In the sentence Because he was being careful, he finished early, the reduced form is Being careful, he finished early. In a similar way, having finished the project, the team went home. Here having finished is a perfect participle, and the word following it tells the reader what happened.

A gerund is different. It is a noun formed from a verb with -ing, such as reading or writing. Gerunds do the work of nouns, while participles do the work of adjectives or adverbs. For example, Reading is my favorite hobby uses a gerund as the subject.

Presenting a report requires confidence. Leaving the room in silence, the speaker showed respect. Opening the window can help the air circulate. In each sentence, the participle phrase is shorter than a full clause, which makes the text faster to read.

Reduced clauses are useful, but they can also cause confusion when the subject is unclear. Good writers check that the participle phrase refers clearly to the subject of the sentence. When you revise your work, try to shorten a clause and then check whether the meaning is still clear.
